clue.text: See 8
Senior citizens love an afterthought

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
a stands in for an, the same indefinite article
PS, postscript, is the afterthought added at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: Pensioners are fond of something added at the last minute.
explanation.definitionFit: OAPs, old age pensioners, is the British shorthand for retired people drawing a state pension.

clue.text: Cook bean, which would be a treat for Homer Simpson

definitions.text: which would be a treat for Homer Simpson

parts.note: to do vegetables or a joint is to cook them
bean and nut are both slang for the head

explanation.surface: Preparing a bean dish would delight the cartoon dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bean' looks like the thing being cooked, but it is slang for the head, as is NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer Simpson's favourite snack is the ring-shaped iced doughnut, spelt the American way in the show.

clue.text: Pug died when stuffed with nuts and stodgy food

indicators.note: in British slang something stuffed is wrecked or done for, so these letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A dog that ate too many nuts met a sorry end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed' seems to describe the pug crammed with nuts, but it signals that PUGDIED and NUTS are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A suet pudding is a heavy steamed British dessert or savoury dish made with beef fat, a classic stodgy dish.

clue.text: With 1A, type that's used in nasty letters

indicators.note: the letters are used inside the run of words that follows, so they lie concealed there

explanation.surface: A typeface favoured for writing poison-pen letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 1A is OLD, so the answer combined with it gives OLD STYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Style is a family of serif typefaces modelled on Renaissance printing, so it is a kind of type.

clue.text: See 11
One of the Beatles is to become less appealing on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to pall is to lose attraction through over-familiarity

explanation.surface: A Beatle starting to lose his charm on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul McCartney was the Beatles' bassist and co-writer with John Lennon.

clue.text: Harry possibly supported by Dec's presenting partner, which is incongruous

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top, held up by the piece below it

parts.note: Prince Harry is Di's son, the son of Diana, Princess of Wales; 'possibly' marks him as one example
Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting double act; Ant is Dec's partner

explanation.surface: Prince Harry propped up by a TV presenter makes an odd pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British television presenting duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dissonant clashes or jars, out of harmony with what surrounds it, so it is incongruous.

clue.text: Kills time essentially with distance runner on evening shifts

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letters of time are taken

parts.note: Mo Farah is the British long-distance runner
working lates means doing the late, evening shifts

explanation.surface: A murderer who keeps time while a runner works nights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time essentially' gives the central IM.
explanation.definitionFit: To immolate is to kill as a sacrifice, especially by burning, so it means kills.

clue.text: Star playing Lady Morgan

indicators.note: an actor playing a part takes on a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes the role of a titled woman called Morgan.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across three lights: 8, 1 and 34, giving the actor's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gary Oldman is an Oscar-winning English film actor, a screen star.

clue.text: With 1A, pre-decimal coin discovered in Lancaster

definitions.meaning: the British coin worth a 240th of a pound before 1971
found within the name ... Lancaster, the model and TV presenter married to Rod Stewart

explanation.walkthrough: 1A is OLD. The second part points to Penny Lancaster, a British model and broadcaster; the blogger was unsure of this reading too.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny is the coin name that pairs with 1A, and also the first name of the celebrity Penny Lancaster.

clue.text: More ghastly Russian spies getting the Queen to eat a certain amount

parts.note: the GRU is Russia's military intelligence agency

indicators.note: the Queen's letters take the next piece inside them, as though eating it

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
some means an unspecified, certain amount

explanation.surface: Spies from Moscow feeding the monarch makes for something grim.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means horrible or ghastly, and this comparative form means more horrible.

clue.text: A good time to be a Harry and score a full round?

definitions.text: A good time to be a Harry

parts.note: a score is twenty
a full round of golf is eighteen holes

explanation.surface: A year when it paid to be called Harry, and to card twenty over a complete round.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2018 Prince Harry married and Harry Kane won the World Cup Golden Boot, among other Harrys' successes.
explanation.definitionFit: The year named here was a notably successful one for several famous people called Harry.

clue.text: Minute number one

definitions.meaning: number one is a childish euphemism for urinating

explanation.definitionFit: Wee means very small in Scots, and is also nursery slang for urine, also called number one.

clue.text: Argument about limits of load in place Columbus set sail from with 1A

definitions.text: place Columbus set sail from with 1A

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A quarrel over the extent of a ship's cargo in the explorer's home port.
explanation.walkthrough: 1A is OLD, giving OLD WORLD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old World is Europe, Africa and Asia, the side of the globe Columbus sailed away from.

clue.text: Fish in the corner

definitions.meaning: fish as a verb, to go fishing with rod and line
a corner is where two lines or walls meet

explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with a hook and line; an angle is also the corner formed where two lines meet.

clue.text: With 1A, Ancien Régime giving command

definitions.meaning: the ancien régime is the French phrase for the old ..., the system of rule before the Revolution

explanation.walkthrough: 1A is OLD, giving OLD ORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is an instruction to be obeyed, and the old order translates the French ancien régime.

clue.text: Time as defined by Einstein in a certain formulation

definitions.note: a period of life or of a century, plural like the answer

indicators.note: a formulation is a way of setting things out, so the scientist's name is set out in a new order

explanation.surface: How Einstein defined time in one of his equations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formulation' suggests E=mc² and relativity, but here it signals a rearrangement of the physicist's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineties are a period of time, whether a decade of a century or a person's age from ninety to ninety-nine.

clue.text: 68-reg Kuga, for example, with stripped gold interior, that's exchanged at midnight

indicators.note: the next piece goes into the interior of the car's letters

parts.note: a car with a 68 registration plate was new in late 2018, and the Kuga is a Ford model

indicators.note: stripped of its outer layer, the word keeps only its inside letters

explanation.surface: A brand-new car with its gold trim removed is traded in late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: At midnight on New Year's Eve, the new year replaces the old one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a swap of new for old, as when the old year gives way to the new at midnight.

clue.text: Mates larking around under canvas in books, with 1A

indicators.note: the friends are under the canvas, so they go inside its letters

parts.note: to be under canvas is to camp in a tent

indicators.note: friends larking around are fooling about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Friends messing about while camping, among a stack of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 1A is OLD, giving OLD TESTAMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament is the first part of the Christian Bible, made up of many books.

clue.text: With 1A, one who painted Mother Cradling Son

indicators.note: the mother's letters hold the next piece as she would hold a baby

parts.note: mater is Latin for mother, used jokingly in English

explanation.surface: An artist who painted a Madonna and Child scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 1A is OLD, giving OLD MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Master is a great European painter from before about 1800, or one of their works.

clue.text: One has certain rights to cover such a shelter with water

indicators.note: the water's letters go around the shelter, covering it

parts.note: making water is passing urine, which is pee
a tent, the kind of shelter from the previous down clue's camping under canvas

explanation.surface: Someone with rights to waterproof a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' looks back to the clue above, where friends are under canvas: such a shelter is a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A patentee holds a patent, which grants exclusive rights to an invention.

clue.text: Frequently leaving Suffolk resort, most depressed

indicators.note: the word for frequently leaves, so it is taken out

parts.note: Lowestoft is a seaside town in Suffolk, an English county on the east coast
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: Often leaving the seaside town leaves someone at their gloomiest.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowestoft is a seaside town in the English county of Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest spirits are the most depressed, low meaning dejected.

clue.text: Bandits regularly thrash around, which is a bit off

indicators.note: the beating's letters go around the picked letters

parts.note: to baste someone is to beat them soundly

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Robbers beating each other up is not quite acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks ADT from Bandits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in bad taste is a bit off, offending decency or good manners.

clue.text: Time had by 1D with 1A

parts.note: 1D is OAPs and 1A is OLD: pensioners are in the period of life called old with the answer

explanation.walkthrough: With 1A this gives OLD AGE, the stage of life pensioners have reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Age is a period of time, and old age is the time of life of senior citizens.

clue.text: With 1A, one's rather timid with Arabian state

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A rather nervous person accompanied by a Gulf nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 1A is OLD, giving OLD WOMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An old woman is a slang term for a fussy, timid or cautious person of either sex.

clue.text: Allude to snaffling cigarette end to make spliff

indicators.note: to snaffle is to grab, so the word takes the next letter inside it

parts.note: to allude to something is to refer to it

indicators.note: the end of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Mentioning pinching a cigarette butt to roll a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a cannabis cigarette, which is also called a spliff.

clue.text: Confronts what you'd expect to see in a regular haunt with 1A

definitions.meaning: to face up to someone is to confront them

definitions.text: what you'd expect to see in a regular haunt with 1A
definitions.meaning: 1A is OLD: old familiar people seen at one's usual haunt

explanation.definitionFit: Faces as a verb means confronts; old faces are the familiar people you meet in your usual pub or haunt.

clue.text: Watery fluid in said space

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A puddle of liquid in a spoken room.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose, so it is a thin bodily fluid.

clue.text: Constant rivals in Glasgow, with 1A

definitions.meaning: ... and constant both mean steadfast, unwavering
the name for Celtic and Rangers, Glasgow's two great rival football clubs

explanation.walkthrough: 1A is OLD. Celtic and Rangers are Glasgow's big football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means steadfast or constant, and the Old Firm is the joint name for Glasgow's rival football clubs.

clue.text: Something recorded by 26, for example, is a mere trifle with 1A

definitions.meaning: 26 is FACES, the Rod Stewart band, who made records of tunes
1A is OLD: something bought for an old ... costs very little

explanation.definitionFit: A song is a recorded track; going for an old song means sold for a trifling amount.

clue.text: Won't dance in more established area with 1A

indicators.note: letters that dance move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to dance in a long-settled district.
explanation.walkthrough: 1A is OLD, giving OLD TOWN; the apostrophe in Won't is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: The old town is the historic, longer-settled heart of a city, as opposed to newer districts.

clue.text: Cleared up as routine do got out of control

indicators.note: a party that got out of control went wild, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An ordinary party went wild, and then everything was sorted out.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron out a problem is to resolve it, so ironed out means cleared up.

clue.text: Statement showing company's not in the red — quite the opposite

indicators.note: the clue first says the colour is not inside the business, a claim the follow-up will flip
the clue first claims the business is not in debt, then flips it, so the colour sits inside the business after all

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm declares it is in profit rather than debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not in the red' reads as a business boast of solvency; 'quite the opposite' turns that round into the containment the solver needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of beliefs, from the Latin for I believe.

clue.text: Middlesex and Derbyshire openers stumped by cricket commentator's complaint

indicators.note: the opening letters of each word, as openers start a cricket innings

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
Aggers is the nickname of Jonathan Agnew, the BBC radio cricket commentator

explanation.surface: Two county teams' opening batsmen dismissed by a broadcaster's ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: Middlesex and Derbyshire are English county cricket sides. 'openers' takes the first letter of all three words, 'and' included.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad staggers is an old name for a brain disorder in horses and cattle, so it is an animal complaint.
